minutes.headline: Board must pick an MBTA Communities zoning compliance option by late June, after public input sessions
minutes.summary: The Planning Board covered chair coverage of the planning office during the land use director's absence, the tight timeline for choosing an MBTA Communities zoning compliance option with a consultant (Community Scale) presenting options May 12th and a decision needed by late June, and endorsed an ANR plan for 60 Cross Road. Several prior decisions were signed, committee reports included the Municipal Building Design Committee's reaffirmed recommendation to demolish the Brooks House and use its existing cost estimate for a town meeting warrant article, and the board approved its March 24 minutes before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board must choose an MBTA Communities zoning compliance option by late June, after a consultant presents options and the board holds additional public information sessions.

The Municipal Building Design Committee reaffirmed a majority recommendation to demolish the Brooks House and will use its existing cost estimate as the town meeting warrant article ask, without a separate vote on that figure.
The board endorsed an ANR plan creating two lots at 60 Cross Road.
The chair is covering extra hours at the planning office while the land use director is unavailable.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities decision sets the zoning option the town will live with under the state law, and the public sessions before June are residents' chance to weigh in before it is locked in.
The Brooks House demolition recommendation and its warrant article will come before town meeting as a dollar ask, using a cost estimate that was not re-voted on by the committee.
The ANR endorsement for 60 Cross Road allows that property to be split into two buildable lots without further Planning Board review.
